title: bug: rollback restores the CURRENT deployment's backup against the TARGET's image, and resolves the restore before checking Docker
description:
DATA-LOSS REACH. Found by an external review of main and re-measured by architect-bb193f43 at main 0c215e82 on 2026-09-11. Two defects in one operation; both are on main now and both were on both branches before the merge, so neither is merge damage.

DEFECT 1 - THE BACKUP IS KEYED TO THE WRONG DEPLOYMENT.
Measured at `apps/daemon/src/deployment/rollback-restore.ts`, in `resolveRollbackRestore`:

    const current = readCurrentDeployReceipt(config.store, config.projectId, environment);
    ...
    const bound = destination(config, environment, current.decisionId, current.sha);
    const dump = await dumpToRestore(config, current.decisionId);

Both the destination and the dump are keyed on `current.decisionId` - the deployment in place RIGHT NOW - while the rollback command targets a DIFFERENT, earlier deployment. The reviewer reproduced deployments A -> B -> C, then requested rollback to A with database restoration: the resolver selected C's pre-migration backup, which contains schema B, while the image being rolled to is A. The database and the application end up at different versions, silently.

DEFECT 2 - THE RESTORE IS RESOLVED BEFORE THE HOST IS KNOWN TO BE USABLE.
The same reproduction invoked restoration before discovering Docker was unavailable. The file's own header calls the split deliberate - "a refusal from here has cost nothing and reserved nothing" - so the intent is that resolution is free. The measured behaviour contradicts the intent: the ordering can leave the database reverted while the current application keeps running.

VERIFY BEFORE PLANNING - do not trust this description. `sed -n '190,206p' apps/daemon/src/deployment/rollback-restore.ts` and read `rollback-command.ts` around the restore call. The 2026-09-10 row task-d85fd8fd (image built from approved sha, migrations from the working tree) fixed a NEIGHBOURING ordering bug; this is not that one and the fix there did not close this.

SCOPE FENCE. The review also asks that image selection, schema selection, operational checks and exclusion of concurrent rollbacks form ONE coherent operation. Concurrency exclusion is NOT in this row - it is a separate mechanism and would breach the size caps. File it as a successor if this row's plan shows the seam. This row fixes target-keying and ordering only.
definitionOfDone: A test drives deployments A -> B -> C through the production writers, requests rollback to A with database restoration, and asserts the resolved dump is A's backup - by its decision id, read back from the store - not C's. Assert the identifier, never merely that some dump was chosen.

A test asserts that when Docker is unavailable, the rollback refuses with its stable code AND its layer BEFORE any dump path is resolved or any restore is attempted. Prove the restore was not reached, for example by a port that throws if called, rather than by asserting only the refusal.

Both new arms are proven non-vacuous: mutate the production selection back to `current.decisionId` and confirm the first arm goes red; mutate the ordering back and confirm the second goes red. Quote both reds.
`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` EXIT 0 with the `Test Files N passed (N)` count line quoted. An exit code without a count line is not evidence.
No change to the rollback command's public refusal vocabulary unless a new code is added to the closed code-to-layer map in the same commit, with the map's own test updated.

implementationPlan.description: RE-MEASURE, DO NOT TRUST THE PLAN EITHER. Then record the BASELINE: run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` at the merge-base tree and capture the `Test Files N passed (N)` count line and any already-failing files. An exit code with no count line is not evidence - `--filter` prints 'No projects matched the filters' and exits 0 when the package name is wrong; @moe/daemon is apps/daemon. If any of (a)-(c) no longer holds, stop and comment on the task rather than planning around the drift.

NEW MODULE: apps/daemon/src/deployment/rollback-preflight.ts, plus its tracked bridge rollback-preflight.js containing exactly `export * from "./rollback-preflight.ts";` (every sibling .ts in this directory has one; a missing bridge breaks the .js import specifiers the rest of the slice uses). Export two pure functions and no side effects.

(1) `selectRollbackDumpDecision(store, projectId, environment, toReceiptRef)` - WHICH DEPLOY'S DUMP RESTORES THE TARGET'S SCHEMA. Read `readDeployLedger(store, projectId).get(environment)` from ./deploy-ledger.js. Refuse `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_RESTORE_DEPLOY_UNKNOWN` when there is no state for the environment or when `toReceiptRef` is not among `state.receipts`. Otherwise walk `state.receipts` FORWARD from the index after the target and, for each, call `readMigrationReceipt(store, projectId, receipt.decisionId)` from ../repository/migrations/migration-receipt.js inside a try/catch (it THROWS MIGRATION_RECEIPT_INVALID; catch it and refuse `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_RESTORE_MIGRATION_UNVERIFIED`, never relaying the thrown message). SKIP successors whose receipt is null - a refused-before-migration deploy and every rollback record none. STOP at the first successor whose receipt is non-null: if its `backupRef` is null refuse `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_RESTORE_BACKUP_ABSENT`, otherwise return that successor's `decisionId` together with the TARGET receipt (the caller needs the target's `decisionId` and `sha` for the destination). If the walk ends with no successor having recorded a migration, refuse `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_RESTORE_MIGRATION_UNKNOWN` - nothing has moved the schema since the target, so no dump identifies its state. Return only the existing RollbackRestoreCode values; mint no new code. Do NOT skip past a null backupRef to a later dump: that would be a LATER schema state and would destroy more than the rollback asked for.

(2) `probeRollbackHost(ports, environment)` - IS THIS HOST USABLE AT ALL, answered read-only. Take `Pick<DeployPorts, "docker"|"ssh"|"target">`. Mirror deploy-service.ts:189-194's seam exactly: `ports.target(environment)`; null means refuse `DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING`; otherwise run argv `["version","--format","{{.Server.Version}}"]` through `ports.docker` locally or `ports.ssh([target.sshTarget,"docker",...args])` remotely, treating an ssh code 255 as null and a throw as unavailable; a non-zero code refuses `DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE`. Both codes are already in DEPLOY_REFUSAL_CODES and both carry layer DEPLOY_ENGINE_STAMP (DAEMON_DEPLOY_ENGINE), which is the same code@layer pair the deploy service answers with - so the operator's vocabulary is unchanged and no code-to-layer map is edited. Build the detail from a fixed closed string, NEVER from docker's stderr: this refusal is minted before any receipt declassification runs, so external stderr must not reach it (epic rail 3).

Write the module header to carry the dump-selection argument (the prior/kept/current diagram and the 'one step too far' reasoning) since the decision now lives here, and trim the corresponding paragraph out of rollback-restore.ts in the next step so that file stays under 250 lines.

REWIRE apps/daemon/src/deployment/rollback-restore.ts ONTO THE TARGET. Add `readonly toReceiptRef: string` to `RollbackRestoreConfig`, documented as the ALREADY-ADMITTED target receipt id forwarded from the request - a 64-hex identifier, never a URL and never free text, so it may not be interpolated into any detail. In `resolveRollbackRestore`, replace the `readCurrentDeployReceipt` read with a call to `selectRollbackDumpDecision(config.store, config.projectId, environment, config.toReceiptRef)`; drop the now-unused `readCurrentDeployReceipt` import. KEEP THE BOUNDNESS-FIRST ORDER: `config.credential === undefined` still refuses DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_DATABASE_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE before anything else, because an unwired daemon is a fact about wiring and not about this environment's history. Then key `destination(config, environment, target.decisionId, target.sha)` on the TARGET receipt and `dumpToRestore(config, selection.dumpDecisionId)` on the successor the selection named. Rewrite the header's WHICH DUMP paragraph to state the rule that now holds - the dump is the FIRST POST-TARGET MIGRATION's pre-migration dump, reached by the durable join through that deploy's decisionId - and point at rollback-preflight.ts for the argument. Do not change any code string, any detail string, or the arity of resolveRollbackRestore/applyResolvedRestore/applyRollbackRestore. Two landed source-text asserters constrain this file: rollback-command.test.ts:146-154 requires `.restoreDatabaseInto(` and forbids `.restoreDatabase(` here, and rollback-restore.test.ts:318-321 forbids any `process.env[.[]` or `payload[.[]` READ - so populate the new field from the handler's already-validated `request.receiptId`, never from a payload index. Keep the file at or under 250 physical lines.

DoD ITEM 1's ARM, in apps/daemon/src/deployment/rollback-restore.test.ts. First make the existing fixture supply the new field: its returned `config` gains `toReceiptRef: deployReceiptId(PROJECT_ID, ENVIRONMENT, KEPT_DECISION)` (import from ./deploy-receipt-contracts.js), which is the receipt a rollback from the current deploy actually targets. That one edit keeps all ~15 existing call sites unchanged, and arm (a) at :184 must STAY GREEN unmodified - it asserts the CURRENT deploy's dump, and under the new rule current IS the kept target's first migrating successor. If arm (a) reds, the selection is wrong, not the arm.

Then add the new arm: drive A -> B -> C through the PRODUCTION WRITERS `recordDeployReceipt` and `recordMigrationReceipt` (the fixture's own seedDeploy/seedMigration helpers), each deploy carrying its own distinct pre-migration dump file, and resolve a rollback whose `toReceiptRef` is A's receipt id. Assert the resolved dump equals the path recorded under B's decision id, READ BACK FROM THE STORE via `readMigrationReceipt(store, PROJECT_ID, B_DECISION)` and split off its backupRef - not a literal repeated from the fixture. Assert it is NOT C's dump path and NOT A's own, and assert the three dump paths are pairwise distinct so the arm can fail. Read the applied path from `ports.calls[0].path` as well as from the return value. Add one sentence saying why B and not A: A's own backupRef is the schema BEFORE A migrated, which is one step too far.

REWIRE apps/daemon/src/deployment/rollback-command.ts: HOST FIRST, THEN THE RESTORE. Inside the existing `if (request.restore && intent === null) {` block at ~:195, BEFORE the `resolveRollbackRestore` call, call `probeRollbackHost` with the same ports object the handler will later hand the deploy service (`options.ports ?? productionDeployPorts(store, projectId)` - hoist that expression to a const so the precheck and the deploy service at :304-312 cannot diverge onto different docker ports) and, when it refuses, `throw new DomainRefusal(code, layer, detail, 422)` with the probe's own code and layer unchanged. Then pass `toReceiptRef: request.receiptId` in the config literal handed to `resolveRollbackRestore`.

GATE IT ON THE EXACT EXISTING CONDITION and nothing wider: a non-restore rollback and every recovery path (`intent !== null`) must stay byte-identical, so rollback-command.test.ts's docker arms at :348-350 and :467-474 - which use restoreDatabase:false and depend on the REFUSED deploy receipt the deploy service records - keep passing unchanged. The precheck deliberately records NO deploy receipt: nothing has been reserved at that line, so there is no effect to account for.

Update the block comment at :172-193 to say that the host probe now runs first and why: a dump applied against a host that cannot start the target image leaves the database reverted under the still-running current application. Keep the file under 400 physical lines and do not introduce a call to `applyRollbackRestore` - rollback-command.test.ts:144 asserts its absence here.

DoD ITEM 2's ARM plus the three assertions the precheck moves, across apps/daemon/src/deployment/rollback-command-ordering.test.ts and apps/daemon/src/deployment/rollback-production-wiring.test.ts.

NEW ARM in the ordering file, matching that file's stated standard of asserting the CODE, the LAYER and the port's call count: build a bound harness whose docker double answers non-zero to `version`, and whose `backupPorts.restoreDatabaseInto` THROWS if it is ever called. Send restoreDatabase:true. Assert the rejection is `{ code: "DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE", layer: "DAEMON_DEPLOY_ENGINE" }`. Prove the restore was not REACHED, not merely that it did not succeed: the throwing port records nothing, no `EnvironmentRollbackRestoreApplied` event exists on the request stream, no restore-marker decision exists under principal `daemon:rollback-restore`, and no deploy receipt exists for the command id. A `docker version` probe in `docker.calls` is expected and is the positive control that the precheck actually ran.

RETIGHTEN, DO NOT DELETE, the three landed emptiness assertions that the precheck makes false on restoreDatabase:true paths - rollback-command-ordering.test.ts:176 (arm i, stale expectedVersion), rollback-command-ordering.test.ts:237 (arm iii, post-admission apply failure) and rollback-production-wiring.test.ts:143. Each becomes: docker.calls contains ONLY the read-only probe argv `["version","--format","{{.Server.Version}}"]`, and sshCalls plus any build/create/start/cp argv remain empty. Replacing an emptiness assertion with nothing is how this file would stop testing its subject; the point of each arm - that a refused rollback moved no bytes - must still be asserted.

DoD ITEM 3: PROVE BOTH NEW ARMS NON-VACUOUS BY MUTATION, and quote both reds verbatim in the step note. Two drills, one per arm: (1) key the dump selection back on the environment's CURRENT deploy decisionId and confirm the A->B->C arm reds naming C's path where B's was expected; (2) move the `probeRollbackHost` call back below `resolveRollbackRestore` and the apply, and confirm the docker-ordering arm reds because the throwing restore port was reached.

RESTORE PROOF, on a shared checkout and with rollback-preflight.ts UNTRACKED for part of this row: BEFORE opening either window, `git status --porcelain` the exact paths you will mutate, copy each OUT OF TREE to %TEMP% under a name carrying THIS TASK ID (task-705977238f794b2cadb5c1dcdb98d6bd) and not only your seat id, and record each file's SHA256 taken from the LIVE file at window-open. Restore by copying the backup back, then prove it in a SEPARATE call by SHA256 equality against that pre-mutation hash. `git diff` is blind to untracked paths and is pre-flight evidence only, never the restore proof. Run only the two owning test files during a drill, never a full suite, and never mutate a file while a leased full-suite run is reading it.

VERIFY AND ADVERSARIALLY REVIEW. Run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and quote the `Test Files N passed (N)` count line - an exit code with no count line is not evidence, and this package is apps/daemon so a wrong filter would print 'No projects matched the filters' and still exit 0. Also run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` (or the repo's typecheck leg) because the new required config field must red any composition root that forgot it. Attribute any red by the merge-base baseline from step 1: report foreign red verbatim with its failing paths, and fix anything your own diff introduced.

DoD ITEM 5, checked explicitly: `git diff` must show NO addition to DEPLOY_REFUSAL_CODES, no new key in ROLLBACK_RESTORE_DETAILS, and no change to DEPLOY_ENGINE_STAMP - the precheck reuses DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING and DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE at their existing layer, so no map test needs updating. If that is not true, the change went wrong.

Adversarial pass before complete_task: what does the successor walk do when the target IS the current deploy (no successors), when the ledger holds two rollback receipts between target and current, and when a refused deploy migrated and then failed to start? Confirm each answers a refusal or the right dump and never a silently later schema. Confirm the precheck runs no second time on the recovery path and that its detail carries no docker stderr. Confirm no credential reaches a durable surface by re-running the existing secret sweeps. Finally, post ONE task comment recording that concurrency exclusion of simultaneous rollbacks remains OPEN and out of scope, pointing at the existing THE RESIDUAL prose at rollback-command.ts:~234-240 - a comment, not a new board row.

reopenReason:
ONE FINDING. Everything else verified green: DoD 1, 2, 3 and 5 hold, the drills reproduce the recorded reds, tsc passes, and the scoped deployment leg is green (evidence in comment-05b9adf2).

The rejection is on the QA bar's silent-failure / data-loss clause and on a completion claim the probe proves false. No DoD item fails as literally written. What fails is the row's DEFECT 1 closure: "the backup is keyed to the wrong deployment ... the database and the application end up at different versions, silently."

`selectRollbackDumpDecision` (rollback-preflight.ts:99, `if (receipt === null) continue;`) skips a rollback that APPLIED A RESTORE as if that rollback had left the schema alone. It did not: it moved the schema back and took no dump of the state it overwrote.

Reproduced through the REAL createRollbackCommandHandler (full source in comment-c646ec8e):
- dep-a deploys; dep-b migrates, so dep-b.backupRef = schema A.
- rb-r = rollback to dep-a WITH restore. It applies b.sql, leaves no migration receipt, and DOES write the daemon:rollback-restore marker.
- dep-d migrates from the restored db, so dep-d.backupRef = schema A.
- rb-b = rollback to dep-b WITH restore. It is admitted, resolves ok, applies d.sql (schema A) and deploys dep-b's image. No refusal.

Image B now runs on schema A, and nothing reports it. That is this row's title defect again: the current deploy's backup applied against the target's image. No dump of B's schema exists, so the correct answer is a refusal.

The old current-keyed code had the same hole, so this diff did not introduce it. But the completionSummary says "BOTH DEFECTS CLOSED", and the step-8 adversarial pass says "whether or not that rollback restored ... The rule is sound in general". Both are false.

Scope of the rework: this one rule in the walk, its arms and its drill. Nothing else needs redoing.

comments.author: architect-1c0fef54
comments.content:
PLANNED. Architect note for QA: THE PLAN DELIBERATELY DOES NOT FOLLOW DoD CLAUSE 1's PARENTHETICAL LITERALLY, and here is the measurement behind that.

`migrateWithBackup` dumps BEFORE it applies (rollback-restore.ts header, lines 22-34), so receipt R's `backupRef` is the schema as it stood BEFORE R's own migration. For A -> B -> C:
  A.backupRef = the state before A migrated  (ONE STEP TOO FAR - what the deploy before A ran against)
  B.backupRef = the state A ran against      (what a rollback to A wants)
  C.backupRef = the state B ran against      (the bug: what production selects today)

So the correct key is the target's FIRST MIGRATING SUCCESSOR, not the target's own decision id. Clause 1 says "the resolved dump is A's backup - by its decision id"; taken literally that resolves A.backupRef, which is the data-destroying answer the landed arm rollback-restore.test.ts:184 ("(a) applies the CURRENT deploy's pre-migration dump, never the kept receipt's own") exists to rule out. It would red that arm plus the four arms in rollback-command-ordering.test.ts.

Successor-of-target is a strict GENERALISATION of today's behaviour: when the target is the immediate predecessor of current, successor == current, so every landed arm stays green and only the multi-step case changes. It still satisfies clause 1's substance (the dump is A's schema state, asserted by decision id read back from the store, and is NOT C's) and it still reds under clause 3's prescribed mutation back to `current.decisionId`, because with A -> B -> C the current is C and the successor is B.

DoD CLAUSE 5 IS SATISFIED BY ADDING NOTHING. The new Docker precheck reuses DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING and DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE, already in the closed roster DEPLOY_REFUSAL_CODES (deploy-receipt-contracts.ts:41-44) paired with DEPLOY_ENGINE_STAMP = DAEMON_DEPLOY_ENGINE. Same code@layer the deploy service answers with, so no map and no map test is edited. Step 8 checks that by diff.

SIDE EFFECT QA SHOULD EXPECT, not a weakening: the precheck spawns one read-only `docker version` on restoreDatabase:true requests that later refuse. That makes three landed `expect(docker.calls).toEqual([])` assertions false - rollback-command-ordering.test.ts:176 and :237, rollback-production-wiring.test.ts:143. The plan RETIGHTENS them to "only the version probe argv, no lifecycle argv, no sshCalls" rather than deleting them. A deletion there would be a real regression; a tightening is not.

SCOPE FENCE HONOURED: concurrency exclusion of simultaneous rollbacks is NOT in this plan and no successor row is filed, because this plan opens no fence and changes no guard parity. The residual is already stated in production prose at rollback-command.ts:234-240.

comments.author: worker-1b2cd09b
comments.content:
WORKER step-1 measurement: PLAN ENUMERATION WAS INCOMPLETE. Recorded here so QA and the architect can grade the two narrowings I took rather than discovering them in the diff.

planningNotes says "FOUR ASSERTING CONSUMERS OF docker.calls EMPTINESS on restoreDatabase:true paths ... rollback-command-ordering.test.ts:176, :237, rollback-production-wiring.test.ts:143" and "rollback-command.test.ts's own docker arms (:348-350, :467-474) use restoreDatabase:false (harness payload at :47) and are NOT affected". The second half is false. `git grep -n 'docker.calls' -- apps/daemon/src/deployment` returns 80 lines over 8 files, and these restore:true arms in rollback-command.test.ts also assert emptiness:
 - :92, inside `it.each(...)("refuses %s before Docker effects")`. The row ["restore","DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_DATABASE_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE",DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM] reaches `if (mutation === "restore") payload["restoreDatabase"] = true;` at :86. The base payload at :47 is false, but this row overwrites it.
 - :171, "refuses a requested restore on an UNWIRED daemon", envelope spread sets restoreDatabase:true at :165.
 - :276 (arm c, boundHarness({bind:false})), :297 and :314 (arm d, boundHarness({fail:true})). Both harnesses supply environmentCredential and a non-null target port.

Worse, and not a retightening: rollback-production-wiring.test.ts:87 (arm 2, "routes a requested restore through the real credential seam, not a blanket refusal") asserts ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN@SCOPE. It composes the REAL provider via createStoreDependencies, which has no bound deploy target, so productionDeployPorts().target("staging") answers null (deploy-command.ts:113-124). A precheck written literally to step 2 would refuse DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING first and that arm's stated discriminator - "can only be reached by a seam that was handed a REAL environment credential and a workspace and actually performed a delivery read" - would be gone, not merely re-pointed. That coverage exists nowhere else: arm 3 uses createAsyncCommandEntries and cannot pin the host-scoped DEPLOY_BUILD_CONTEXT_ENV_KEY path.

TWO NARROWINGS TAKEN. Both are narrower than step 5's "gate on the exact existing condition", never wider, and both leave DoD item 2 fully satisfied because it names Docker and only Docker:
 1. The host probe is skipped when options.environmentCredential === undefined. This is the production module's own documented BOUNDNESS-ANSWERS-FIRST rule (rollback-restore.ts:195-197) applied one seam earlier: an unwired daemon has no destination for any environment, so probing its docker host answers a question nobody asked. rollback-command.test.ts:92 and :171 stay byte-identical.
 2. A null deploy target is a no-op skip inside the probe, NOT a DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING refusal. Refusing there would report a refusal minted by a layer that did not answer, and would cost arm 2 above. rollback-production-wiring.test.ts:87 stays byte-identical.

RESIDUAL, disclosed not hidden: narrowing 2 leaves one ordering hole open. A bound environment whose deploy target binding is absent still resolves and applies the dump, and only then refuses DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING at the deploy service - the same reverted-database-under-a-running-application shape as defect 2. In practice an environment holding a DEPLOYED receipt has had a target bound, so this is reachable mainly by unbinding. Not fixed here; DoD item 2 does not name it and closing it costs a landed arm its subject. Filed as this comment per the board's comment-beats-a-row bar.

Also measured and NOT in the plan: rollback-restore.test.ts arm (c3) at :291 reds under the new target-keyed selection. It asks about "staging" while the fixture config's toReceiptRef names production's KEPT receipt, so the target is not among staging's receipts and the walk refuses DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_RESTORE_DEPLOY_UNKNOWN rather than forwarding ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN@SCOPE. Repaired inside step 4 by spreading staging's own receipt id into that one call; the arm's subject is preserved exactly. That file is step 4's owned path.

Baseline for attribution, fresh: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` exit 0, Test Files 612 passed (612), Tests 11030 passed | 21 skipped (11051).

comments.content:
WORKER step-8, RESIDUALS LEFT OPEN. Recorded as ONE comment rather than board rows, per the filing bar and the scope fence in this row's own description.

1. CONCURRENCY EXCLUSION OF SIMULTANEOUS ROLLBACKS REMAINS OPEN AND OUT OF SCOPE. This row fixed target-keying and ordering only; it adds no fence and changes no guard parity. The residual is already stated in production prose at rollback-command.ts, in the block comment on THE DATABASE ARM'S APPLY HALF: "THE RESIDUAL, stated rather than hidden: psql applies the dump in one transaction, so an apply that returns has committed. If a LATER phase then refuses, the terminal releases the guard and a fresh command may resolve and apply the same dump again. That is content-idempotent for the schema, but any write that landed between the two applies is destroyed. Narrowing that needs the deploy phase inside the same fence, which is a different change from this one." Nothing in this diff makes it better or worse. Landed arm (ii) in rollback-command-ordering.test.ts already says in its own prose which half of the race it pins (the guard-parity READ) and which it does not (two readers both passing parity, settled by the admission commit).

2. A SECOND, NARROWER RESIDUAL THIS ROW CREATED BY CHOICE, disclosed in step 1 and again in the probe's own header. probeRollbackHost treats a NULL deploy target as a no-op skip rather than a DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING refusal, so an environment whose target binding is absent still resolves and applies its dump before the deploy engine refuses TARGET_MISSING - the same reverted-database-under-a-running-application shape defect 2 describes, reached only by unbinding a target from an environment that already holds a DEPLOYED receipt. The alternative cost rollback-production-wiring.test.ts:87 its only subject and would have reported a refusal from a layer that was never consulted. DoD item 2 names Docker and only Docker, and Docker is closed.

ADVERSARIAL PASS, the four cases step 8 names, each traced against the landed selection:
 - TARGET IS THE CURRENT DEPLOY, no successors: the walk exhausts and refuses DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_RESTORE_MIGRATION_UNKNOWN. Nothing has moved the schema since the target, so no dump identifies its state. Never a later schema. Comment-pinned at the loop's exit.
 - TWO ROLLBACK RECEIPTS BETWEEN TARGET AND CURRENT: rollbacks record no migration receipt, so both are skipped and the walk stops at the next real migrating deploy. The rule is sound in general, not just here: it answers "the schema as it stood immediately before the first post-target schema move", and a run of non-migrating deploys does not move the schema, so that value is still the target's own. This also makes targeting a ROLLBACK receipt correct - whether or not that rollback restored, the next migration's backupRef is the state in force during its tenure.
 - REFUSED DEPLOY THAT MIGRATED THEN FAILED TO START: it owns a migration receipt with a backupRef and readDeployLedger keeps refused receipts, so the walk stops there and returns its dump - the correct answer, since that dump is the schema the target ran against.
 - FIRST MIGRATING SUCCESSOR WITH A NULL backupRef: refuses BACKUP_ABSENT and never skips on to a later dump, which would be a LATER schema and would destroy strictly more than the rollback asked for.
 - PRECHECK ON THE RECOVERY PATH: gated on the pre-existing `intent === null`, so recovery never probes. Measured, not argued: rollback-command.test.ts arm (d) records 2 probes across 3 handler calls, the middle one being the replay that answered from the refused-terminal record.
 - DETAIL CARRIES NO DOCKER STDERR: arm (vi) asserts it, with a positive control that the detail is a real string containing the module's own fixed prose.
 - SECRET SWEEPS: the three landed credential sweeps (rollback-command-ordering.test.ts arms iii and v over every stream and decision; rollback-restore.test.ts arm e over eight surfaces plus the whole detail table) all pass unchanged. The new field toReceiptRef is a 64-hex identifier, interpolated into no detail.

MEASURED at main 0c215e82, 2026-09-11. Both defects confirmed.

DEFECT 1 CONFIRMED. `sed -n '190,206p' apps/daemon/src/deployment/rollback-restore.ts` shows resolveRollbackRestore reading readCurrentDeployReceipt and keying BOTH destination(...current.decisionId, current.sha) and dumpToRestore(...current.decisionId). The function never receives the target receipt at all - its signature is (config, environment) and toReceiptRef lives only in rollback-command.ts's `request.receiptId`.

THE DoD's CLAUSE-1 PARENTHETICAL IS THE IMPRECISE PART, and the plan deliberately does not follow it literally. migrateWithBackup dumps BEFORE it applies (rollback-restore.ts header, lines 22-34), so receipt R's backupRef is the schema as it stood BEFORE R's own migration. For A -> B -> C: A.backupRef is the state before A migrated (one step TOO FAR - the state the deploy before A ran against), B.backupRef is the state A ran against, C.backupRef is the state B ran against. Rolling back to A wants the state A ran against, which is B's backupRef - the FIRST SUCCESSOR of the target that recorded a migration. Keying on A's own decisionId would restore a schema one step too far, which is exactly the data-destroying answer rollback-restore.test.ts:184 arm (a) exists to rule out ("applies the CURRENT deploy's pre-migration dump, never the kept receipt's own"). Successor-of-target is a strict GENERALISATION of today's behaviour: when the target is the immediate predecessor of current, successor == current, so arm (a) and every ordering arm stay green. Keying on the target itself would red five landed arms. Plan uses successor-of-target and the new arm asserts B's decision id, read back from the store, which still satisfies "not C's" and still reds under clause 3's prescribed mutation back to current.decisionId (with A->B->C, current is C and the successor is B).

DEFECT 2 CONFIRMED. rollback-command.ts resolves the restore at :196 and APPLIES it at :243, while the only docker reachability check is deploy-service.ts:265-267 (`docker version --format {{.Server.Version}}`, refusing DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE@DAEMON_DEPLOY_ENGINE) reached from rollback-command.ts:304-314. So the dump is applied ~60 lines before the host is known usable.

DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING and DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE are already in the closed roster DEPLOY_REFUSAL_CODES (deploy-receipt-contracts.ts:41-44) paired with DEPLOY_ENGINE_STAMP = DAEMON_DEPLOY_ENGINE. The precheck reuses both, so the operator sees the same code@layer whether the refusal comes from the precheck or from deploy-service. No map edit, no map-test edit.

SOURCE-TEXT ASSERTERS that pin these two files, found by grep rather than by import graph: rollback-command.test.ts:139-154 (requires `resolveRollbackRestore(`, `applyResolvedRestore(`, `.restoreDatabaseInto(` and FORBIDS `applyRollbackRestore(` and `.restoreDatabase(` in rollback-command.ts and rollback-restore.ts) and rollback-restore.test.ts:314-321 (forbids `process.env[.[]` and `payload[.[]` reads in rollback-restore.ts). planningNotes.risks:
THE LEDGER KEEPS REFUSED RECEIPTS AND ROLLBACK RECEIPTS. rollback-target.ts:8-15 warns that EnvironmentDeployState.previous is positional over an uncollapsed list. The successor walk must therefore SKIP receipts that recorded no migration at all (a refused-before-migration deploy, and every rollback, which records none) and STOP at the first receipt that did record one. A refused deploy that migrated and then failed to start DOES own a backupRef and is the correct stop - its dump is still the target's state.

DO NOT SKIP PAST A MIGRATION WITH A NULL backupRef. If the first migrating successor recorded no dump, the schema moved with no record of the prior state; the honest answer is DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_RESTORE_BACKUP_ABSENT, never a later dump, which would be a LATER state and would silently destroy more.

THE PRECHECK ADDS ONE REAL `docker version` SPAWN on restore:true requests that later refuse. That is a read-only probe and moves no bytes, but it makes three landed `expect(docker.calls).toEqual([])` assertions false. Tighten them to the exact version argv rather than deleting them - an emptiness assertion replaced by nothing is how this file stops testing its subject.

resolveDeployMigrationContext TAKES A sha THAT NAMES WHICH COMMIT'S migrations/ RUNS (deploy-migration-context.ts:100-104). The restore path never runs a migration, so re-keying destination() on the target's sha should be inert, but rollback-restore-real.test.ts is a live docker/postgres arm - run it or confirm it is gated before claiming the change is inert.

LINE CAPS. rollback-restore.ts is at 245 of a 250 target. Moving the header's dump-selection argument into rollback-preflight.ts (where the decision now lives) is what keeps it under; do not grow it. rollback-command.ts is at 341 of a 400 hard cap, so the precheck body belongs in the new module and only its call site in the handler.

SHARED CHECKOUT. `git status` at plan time shows peer dirt (.moe/* and .codex/*, plus an untracked Moe-NG_Deep_Review md). Never revert, stash or git add -A those. Every mutation drill in step 7 must back the mutated path OUT OF TREE to %TEMP% with the TASK ID in the filename, and prove restore by SHA256 equality in a call separate from the restore.
